## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:pass`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:pass` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer

```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Lane-label provisioning is correctly gated, fails closed, surfaces every forge write, preserves SPEC-039/AC-10 behavior and all six MinSpec invariants, and is covered by thorough new tests.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

```
blocking: 0
summary: No security issues: gh calls use argv arrays (no injection), no new deps, no secrets, and the single new forge write (docs-lane label create) is consent-gated and confined to the exact label.
findings:
- info packages/minspec/src/commands/commit-on-approve.ts:364 (laneWorkflowPresent) — The provision gate trusts the on-disk presence of .github/workflows/docs-lane.yml, so a hostile repo checkout could plant that file to induce a one-time `docs-lane` label creation. Non-blocking: it still requires the user's consented push and authenticated gh, and the only effect is creating one benign label — negligible impact, noted for completeness rather than as a defect to fix.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

This is an outward-facing behavioural change — MinSpec now WRITES a label object to an adopter's forge — that narrows the long-stated 'MinSpec never creates/edits/reads a forge label' property and is self-labelled T3 in the tests, yet the diff carries no DR recording the decision (why cross that line, boundary/consent rationale) and no spec update. CLAUDE.md's traceability convention (DRs = why we …
```
- info packages/minspec/src/commands/commit-on-approve.ts:366-372 — Blast-radius edge (benign, handled): laneWorkflowPresent() checks the LOCAL checkout for .github/workflows/docs-lane.yml, but the label create targets the forge repo resolved by cwd/slug. In a fork-PR scenario the local fork may carry the workflow while the PR base is an upstream repo the contributor cannot mutate. This degrades safely — gh returns 403 and the flow falls to the manual surface naming the label (covered by the 'cannot create' test) — so no harmful write occurs. Noting only becaus…
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Every behavior/scope claim is backed by cited code or a real test that exercises it; no unproven claim, false status, or vacuous test.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:blocked`

> ⏳ **The AI reviewer could not run — this is NOT a review of your code.**
>
> Almost always the **Claude subscription session quota** is exhausted (also possible: rate-limit / overload). The required `ai-review` check is `action_required` — it blocks merge only because un-reviewed code must not land — and it **re-runs automatically** when the quota window resets (the `ai-review-retry` workflow).
>
> **Options:**
> 1. **Wait** for the quota window to reset — the retry workflow re-reviews automatically.
> 2. **Fail over to PAYG API** — set repo variable `AI_REVIEW_FAILOVER=payg` + secret `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; re-runs then use pay-as-you-go instead of the subscription quota.
> 3. Re-run the `ai-review` workflow manually once quota is back.

<details><summary>reviewer output (redacted — may include the reset time)</summary>

```
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_BEGIN
reason: quota
evidence: NONE (reason is inferred, not observed)
classified_via: stdout(strict)
stderr_bytes: 0
stdout_bytes: 25
detail: |
  (no diagnostic text on either stream — see #1630)
REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE_END
```
</details>

_Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]`. Transient/quota failures are surfaced as `ai-review:blocked` (distinct from `ai-review:changes`) so a token outage never masquerades as a code-review verdict._

commits.messageBody:
…very adopter

Approving SPEC-003/004/005 in voip-sms-inbox ended in an "Open PR" toast, a
hand-made PR with an empty body, and a manual merge (voip-sms-inbox #107-#109).
The same act in this repository lands on its own: MinSpec opens the PR with the
docs-lane label and the lane workflow arms auto-merge (#2088).

Root cause: openApprovalPr passes --label docs-lane to gh pr create for every
lane-eligible approval, and gh refuses to create any pull request when a named
label does not exist in the repository ("could not add label: 'docs-lane' not
found", verified with --dry-run against voip-sms-inbox); MinSpec scaffolds the
docs-lane workflow into adopters but nothing provisions the label it gates on
(ai-review.yml self-heals its own labels, the lane workflow cannot because it
only runs on a PR that already carries its label), and openPullRequest
classified the refusal as a terminal `failed`, so the flow fell to the manual
"Open PR" surface and the hand-made PR could never ride the lane.

The input that differs between the two repositories is the docs-lane label
object: AIClarityAU/minspec has it, AIClarityAU/voip-sms-inbox never did. It is
not config: the extension reads neither autoMerge nor autonomy from
.minspec/config.json.

Fix:
- approval-pr.ts: an opt-in provisionLaneLabel on openPullRequest. A refusal
  naming DOCS_LANE_LABEL creates that one label (never --force, never any
  other name) and retries the create once; a missing label is reported as
  missingLabel rather than an anonymous failure. SPEC-039's classification
  order is unchanged and it does not opt in.
- commit-on-approve.ts: the approval flow opts in only when the PR carries the
  lane label and the checkout has .github/workflows/docs-lane.yml. The toast
  says when the label was created, and a failure names the missing label.
- The labels.md template and the approvalPr setting text state this one
  exception to "MinSpec never creates a label".

Harden: the T0 label scan could not see argv-form gh calls, which is how every
gh call here is written; it now does, and pins the single sanctioned call
site. A new parity test runs the same approval against a fake forge with and
without the label, on both the protected-branch and the push path, and
asserts identical outcomes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

…nto SPEC-050's design

The ai-review Architect blocked #2259 on two findings. This answers both
without changing behaviour.

Missing decision record: DR-098 (proposed) records why the approval flow
may create MinSpec's own missing docs-lane label, the six conditions that
bound the write, the consent reasoning (consent to push an approval covers
the one label its pull request needs, under DR-071's five conditions, and
nothing wider), the narrowing of the shipped labels.md statement, and the
alternatives rejected. INDEX.md regenerated.

Scope beyond SPEC-050 (silent approval PR): its design.md and tasks.md
gain the provisioning design, its tests and its task block. requirements.md
is left alone because its body is inside the approval hash; its wording is
tracked in #2330, following DR-078's precedent that the decision record is
the authority until the requirements catch up. The two test headers now say
their T1 and T3 are test tiers, not the SDD ceremony tier the review read
them as.

Root cause: the T0 pin in labels-template.test.ts fixed WHERE the one
sanctioned label write may happen but never asserted that the write had a
decision record, so the capability could ship with none. The new test
fails unless approval-pr.ts cites DR-098, DR-098 is in force and names the
seam, and SPEC-050's design covers provisionLaneLabel; four mutations
(no DR file, no code citation, design without the section, DR superseded)
each fail it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
